title: String Parsing: Extract Structured Data from Concatenated Field
description:
A `raw_contacts` table stores contact data as a single pipe-delimited string in the format `FirstName|LastName|email@domain.com|phone`. **Parse each record** to extract: first name, last name, full email, email username (part before `@`), email domain (part after `@`), and phone number. Additionally, flag any contacts whose email domain is a `.com` domain.

**Table: raw_contacts**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| contact_id | INT |
| raw_data | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `contact_id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `username`, `domain`, `phone`, `is_com_domain` (boolean). Order by `contact_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE raw_contacts (contact_id INT, raw_data VARCHAR); INSERT INTO raw_contacts VALUES (1,'John|Doe|john.doe@gmail.com|555-1234'),(2,'Jane|Smith|jane.smith@yahoo.com|555-5678'),(3,'Bob|Johnson|bob.j@company.org|555-9012'),(4,'Alice|Williams|alice.w@startup.io|555-3456'),(5,'Charlie|Brown|c.brown@enterprise.net|555-7890'),(6,'Diana|Prince|d.prince@corp.com|555-2345'),(7,'Eve|Adams|eve@personal.me|555-6789'),(8,'Frank|Miller|frank.miller@business.com|555-0123');
solution_sql: SELECT contact_id, SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 1) AS first_name, SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 2) AS last_name, SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 3) AS email, SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 3), '@', 1) AS username, SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 3), '@', 2) AS domain, SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 4) AS phone, CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 3), '@', 2) LIKE '%.com' THEN true ELSE false END AS is_com_domain FROM raw_contacts ORDER BY contact_id

test_cases.description: Parsed structured fields from pipe-delimited raw contact data

hints: SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', N) extracts the Nth field (1-indexed) from a pipe-delimited string. Use it to pull first_name (1), last_name (2), email (3), and phone (4).

To extract the username and domain from the email, nest SPLIT_PART calls: SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(raw_data, '|', 3), '@', 1) gives the part before '@', and SPLIT_PART(..., '@', 2) gives the domain. Use LIKE '%.com' on the domain to flag commercial email addresses.
explanation: SPLIT_PART is PostgreSQL's function to extract a specific token from a delimited string (equivalent to Python's split()[n]). Nesting two SPLIT_PART calls extracts nested structure: first split by '|' to get the email field, then split by '@' to separate username from domain. The is_com_domain flag uses a LIKE '%.com' pattern on the extracted domain — contacts 1, 2, 6, and 8 have .com domains. This string-parsing pattern is ubiquitous in data engineering when loading CSVs, log files, or legacy system exports where data is stored denormalized in a single column. In production, this logic would live in a staging transform layer.
